I started OpenCode in the subdirectory ~/Projects/lean-projects/lean-playground, then managed to generate correct Lean proofs of the two theorems above. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP took 21 minutes and 22 seconds to prove the first theorem, generating 34,212 tokens.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP's proof of the first theorem

import Mathlib.Data.Set.Basic

namespace Set

open Function

universe u

theorem ext' {α : Type u} {A B : Set α} (h : ∃ (f : A → B), Surjective f ∧
    ∀ (a : A), ∃ (haB : a.val ∈ B), f a = ⟨a.val, haB⟩) : A = B := by
  rcases h with ⟨f, hf_surj, hf_def⟩
  apply Set.ext
  intro x
  constructor
  · intro hx
    rcases hf_def ⟨x, hx⟩ with ⟨haB, _⟩
    exact haB
  · intro hx
    rcases hf_surj ⟨x, hx⟩ with ⟨a, ha⟩
    have : ↑a = x := by
      obtain ⟨a_prop, hf⟩ := hf_def a
      rw [hf] at ha
      exact congrArg Subtype.val ha
    exact this ▸ a.property

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP also succeeded in proving the second theorem; it took 1 hour, 11 minutes, and 9 seconds to complete the proof, generating 116,825 tokens.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP's proof of the second theorem

import Mathlib.Order.WellFounded

/-- If `a` is accessible through a binary relation `r`, then every descending chain starting from
`a` ends at a minimal element of a type `α` with respect to `r`. -/
theorem Acc.descending_chain_ends_at_min_of_acc {α : Sort u} {r : α → α → Prop} {a : α}
    (acc : Acc r a) {f : Nat → α}
    (hsta : f 0 = a)
    (hcon : ∀ ⦃n : Nat⦄, (∀ (y : α), ¬r y (f n)) → f (n + 1) = f n)
    (hdes : ∀ ⦃n : Nat⦄, (¬∀ (y : α), ¬r y (f n)) → r (f (n + 1)) (f n)) :
    ∃ (c : Nat),
      (∀ ⦃y : α⦄, ¬r y (f c)) ∧
      (∀ ⦃n : Nat⦄, n < c → r (f (n + 1)) (f n)) ∧
      ∀ ⦃m : Nat⦄, c ≤ m → f m = f c := by
  let P : α → Prop := fun x =>
    ∀ (g : Nat → α), g 0 = x →
      (∀ ⦃n⦄, (∀ z, ¬r z (g n)) → g (n + 1) = g n) →
      (∀ ⦃n⦄, (¬∀ z, ¬r z (g n)) → r (g (n + 1)) (g n)) →
      ∃ c, (∀ y, ¬r y (g c)) ∧ (∀ n < c, r (g (n + 1)) (g n)) ∧ (∀ m ≥ c, g m = g c)
  have step : ∀ x (H : ∀ y, r y x → Acc r y) (ih : ∀ y, r y x → P y), P x := fun x H ih => fun g gsta hgcon hgdes => by
    classical
    by_cases hmin : ∀ z, ¬r z x
    · use 0
      constructor
      · intro y hy
        apply hmin
        rw [gsta] at *
        exact hy
      · constructor
        · intro n hn
          omega
        · intro m
          have h_const_all : ∀ n, g n = g 0 := by
            intro n
            induction n with
            | zero => rfl
             | succ n ih =>
              have h_const : g (n + 1) = g n := by
                have h_all_min : ∀ z, ¬r z (g n) := by
                  intro z hz
                  have hz0 : r z (g 0) := by rw [← ih]; exact hz
                  rw [gsta] at hz0
                  exact hmin z hz0
                exact hgcon h_all_min
              rw [h_const, ih]
          exact fun _ => h_const_all m
    · have hnotmin : ¬∀ z, ¬r z x := hmin
      have hg0_eq_x : g 0 = x := gsta
      have hnotmin_g0 : ¬∀ z, ¬r z (g 0) := by
        intro h
        apply hnotmin
        intro z hz
        rw [hg0_eq_x] at *
        exact h z hz
      have hdesc : r (g 1) (g 0) := hgdes hnotmin_g0
      have hgcon' : ∀ ⦃n⦄, (∀ z, ¬r z (g (n + 1))) → g (n + 2) = g (n + 1) := by
        intro n hy
        have := hgcon hy
        simpa using this
      have hgdes' : ∀ ⦃n⦄, (¬∀ z, ¬r z (g (n + 1))) → r (g (n + 2)) (g (n + 1)) := by
        intro n hy
        have := hgdes hy
        simpa using this
      let g' : Nat → α := fun n => g (n + 1)
      have g'_start : g' 0 = g 1 := by rfl
      have hdesc_eq : r (g 1) x := by
        rw [hg0_eq_x] at *
        exact hdesc
      have ih_result : ∃ c', (∀ y, ¬r y (g' c')) ∧ (∀ n < c', r (g' (n + 1)) (g' n)) ∧ (∀ m ≥ c', g' m = g' c') :=
        ih (g 1) hdesc_eq g' g'_start hgcon' hgdes'
      rcases ih_result with ⟨c', hmin', hdes', hconst'⟩
      use c' + 1
      constructor
      · intro y hy
        exact hmin' y hy
      · constructor
        · intro n hn
          by_cases hn0 : n = 0
          · rw [hn0]
            have hnotmin0 : ¬∀ z, ¬r z (g 0) := by
              intro h
              apply hmin
              intro z hz
              have hz' : r z (g 0) := by
                rw [← hg0_eq_x] at hz
                exact hz
              exact h z hz'
            have hdesc' : r (g 1) (g 0) := hgdes hnotmin0
            simpa using hdesc'
          · have hn1 : n ≥ 1 := by omega
            have hn' : n - 1 < c' := by omega
            have h : r (g' ((n - 1) + 1)) (g' (n - 1)) := hdes' (n - 1) hn'
            simpa [g', hn1] using h
        · intro m hm
          have hm1 : m ≥ 1 := by omega
          have hmi : m - 1 ≥ c' := by omega
          have h : g ((m - 1) + 1) = g (c' + 1) := hconst' (m - 1) hmi
          simpa [hm1] using h
  have h_acc_P : P a := @Acc.rec α r (fun x _ => P x) step a acc
  rcases h_acc_P f hsta hcon hdes with ⟨c, hmin, hdes, hconst⟩
  exact ⟨c, hmin, hdes, hconst⟩

The point here is that you can use an average desktop computer to run a 35B MoE model. Then, you can make the model prove basic theorems in Lean. I didn’t know this was possible.
